sets.relationshipLabel: kitchen tool and the action it exists to perform
sets.explanation: A whisk exists to beat and a grater exists to shred — each tool is defined by the single motion it's built for.

sets.relationshipLabel: informal household term becomes the formal/specific appliance name
sets.explanation: You call it a fridge, but its formal name is refrigerator; you call it a freezer, but the standalone unit is a deep freezer — each pair moves from everyday speech to the precise term.

sets.relationshipLabel: fixture fastened to shield or complete the surface it's mounted to
sets.explanation: A backsplash is fastened to protect the wall behind it, and a toe-kick is fastened to finish off the cabinet base beneath it — each fixture exists to cover what it's attached to.

sets.relationshipLabel: same kind of cookware, smaller then larger
sets.explanation: A saucepan scales up to a stockpot and a ramekin scales up to a roasting pan — same category of vessel, just sized differently.

glossary.definition: A short recessed strip of trim near the floor, set back so you can stand close without stubbing your toes.

definitions.definition: A wire loop tool you swirl through eggs or cream to mix in air and smooth out lumps.
To stir something fast and hard, usually to mix ingredients or add fluffiness.
A tool with sharp little holes you rub food across to turn it into fine bits.
To tear or grind something into thin strips or small pieces.
The everyday name for the cold box in your kitchen that keeps food from spoiling.
The full, proper name for the appliance that chills your food to keep it fresh.
The icy-cold compartment or unit where you store food to keep it frozen solid.
A standalone freezing unit, bigger and colder than a regular one, for long-term storage.
The panel behind your stove or sink that keeps splashes and grease off the wall.
The flat vertical surface that makes up the sides of a room.
A short recessed strip of trim near the floor, set back so you can stand close without stubbing your toes.
The bottom part of a cabinet that sits on the floor and holds everything up.
A small deep pot with a handle, good for sauces, soups, or boiling small batches.
A big tall pot for making stock, soup, or boiling large amounts of food at once.
A small individual dish for baking or serving single portions like custard.
A large sturdy pan for roasting big cuts of meat or whole dishes in the oven.
